source: Figma Prism-Visual-ID-Exploration frame Option 10 (90:710). Names approved in Phase 0. Hex lives only in this file.

eclipse.role: geometry, type, and legacy states; never blurred

mist.role: ground and the negative space between shapes

filter_id.rule: Ids are unique across the whole document.

origin.from_focal: A composition may move the origin to its focal point when the light relation is from-focal.

fan.light_bands: Bands higher in the composition use angles near upper. Lower bands use angles near lower. Interpolate between.
fan.geometry_rule: Fan angles are the default for light direction. Geometric shapes may use any angles, as long as a composition uses one consistent shape system and the light's edges share its angles.

light.rule: Use the pairs already in that graphic. One mark uses one pair. Do not apply every pair to every instance. A ray's inner and outer colors always come from one pair: yellow/red (flare/ember) or blue/purple (sky/violet).
light.tonality: Match the washed rays in Color Concept 04, not the flat swatches. High-key, pale, edges dissolved into mist. No gloss, no hard silhouette.

pairs.name: gold/red
pairs.flag: Ember is lighter and more orange than #C00105. Approved by Miranda as the light-mode red rim (2026-09-28).

pairs.name: blue/purple
pairs.flag: Approved by Miranda (2026-09-28): blue's outer is purple. Sky is also the cyan/orange inner, so the two pairs share an inner in light mode.

geometry_line.rule: All lines and dashes are hairline weight with rounded ends, one solid flat color each. Crisp, never blurred, never gradient.
geometry_line.weight: 1 px at 1x (about 1/1000 of the image's short side). The lightest stroke on the page, lighter than the thinnest stroke in body type. Say 'a single-pixel hairline' in prompts, never a pixel count above 1.
geometry_line.color_rule: Lines use only the lighter inner colors of the ray pairs (flare, sky). Never ember or violet for a line; the darker outer colors read flat as lines and belong to the diffused rim of light.

rendering_rule: Anything with a hard edge is one solid flat color. Anything with a gradient or more than one color is diffused light with soft, blurred edges. Never a crisp edge around a gradient. Light is smooth: clean continuous gradients with no grain, noise, speckle, dithering, or texture.
